runtime_verify.note: Playwright screenshots against next dev on :3000 at each increment: full /about page after the portrait swap (jasper-fu-about.jpg renders correctly, cleanly cropped under the name/thesis overlay gradient), the full page again after Quick Facts and pull-quotes render (navy .stat-card--primary + two .stat-card cards, .quote-card pull-quotes all visually correct against the site's real palette), the .faq-list both closed (three rows, + markers) and after clicking the first <summary> to open it (marker flips to −, answer text reveals), a full-page pass after the press-gallery section was removed, and desktop (1400px) plus mobile (390px) passes after the header/portrait restyle — the About label now reads as a small sky mono eyebrow, the cash-to-digital quote leads at display scale, the portrait renders clean with no scrim, and the headline reflows to 6 lines on mobile without overflow. Then again after the hero-showcase rebuild, where a screenshot showed the broadcast chyron still colliding with the name: a Playwright computed-style probe found the img box at 1280x720 with aspect-ratio reported as 12/5 but ignored, because the width/height attributes are presentational hints and, with width:100% also set, both axes were definite. Adding height:auto fixed it — re-probed at 1280x533 (ratio 2.4) and re-shot at 1400px and 390px, chyron fully cropped, name and glass stat pill sitting clean on the still, caption dropping below the image on mobile. No console errors in any pass. Confirms not just DOM correctness but actual visual rendering.

notes: About page overhaul: added trust/credibility content that already existed in lib/copy.ts as drafted-but-unwired constants (quickFacts, pullQuotes, aboutFaqs), plus a closing CTA, none of it previously rendered anywhere. A press/public-appearance photo gallery (aboutGalleryPhotos + .proof-gallery) was built and then removed at the user's direction before finishing: it duplicated the dedicated /press route, and its only available source images were low-resolution video stills that cropped badly when scaled to full width. It was reverted in full — constant, type, guards, unit tests, DOM helper, and CSS — rather than left as an unrendered constant, since orphaned unused content constants are an existing problem in this repo, not a pattern worth adding to. Swapped the About portrait from the literal /portraits/jasper-fu-placeholder.jpg (a file lib/hero.ts itself names RETIRED_HERO_PORTRAIT) to the real, unused /portraits/jasper-fu-about.jpg, correcting the img height metadata from the old placeholder's 864 to the new file's actual 975. Added parseCareerTimeline/parseCredentials guards for two lists that were already live on the page but previously unguarded. New guards mirror the existing FactSheetRow/assertFactSheetRow/parseFactSheet pattern exactly: trim -> per-field required checks -> placeholder-string rejection -> return, with MIN/MAX bounds and uniqueness checks on the array-level parse function. aboutFaqs ships only its first 3 (of 4) questions — assertAboutFaq explicitly rejects any answer starting with "Definition pending", so the drafted-but-unfinished 4th question ("What does programmable money mean?") cannot ship even if ABOUT_FAQ_PUBLISHED_COUNT is bumped without first replacing that stub; a unit test proves the future one-line bump to 4 works once given real copy. Unique errors per guard: career timeline / credentials — item required vs item is a placeholder vs below-min vs above-max vs items must each be unique; quick facts — label required vs {label} value required vs {label} detail required vs {label} is a placeholder vs below-min vs above-max vs labels must each be unique; pull-quotes — quote required vs quote is a placeholder vs below-min vs above-max vs quotes must each be unique; about FAQ — question required vs {question} answer required vs {question} answer is still a pending stub vs count below 1 vs count exceeds available questions vs questions must each be unique. Three pre-existing tests in app/public-routes.test.tsx collided with content that is now intentionally published and were updated accordingly: verifyAboutAbsences() no longer asserts "Who is David Akers?" absent; the test formerly titled "omits 250-word-only copy, approved lengths, FAQ, and the co-founder pair" was renamed and had its now-false FAQ/co-founder assertions removed (its unrelated 250-word-only assertions are untouched and still pass); "omits the unused pull-quote list from About" was replaced with a positive "surfaces the pull-quote list on About" test. Confirmed unaffected: app/page.test.tsx's homeQuote/pullQuotes[0] absence check is scoped to the home page, which this feature does not touch, and was re-run green. Access control is N/A for every new guard — all About content is public with no auth. Header/portrait restyle: the About page was visually weak against the home hero, so the oversized gold label (2x eyebrow scale), the navy rule beneath it, and the gold-bordered callout treatment of the opening quote were all retired; the label now matches the sitewide sky mono eyebrow and the quote leads at display scale (clamp(1.7rem, 3.1vw, 2.6rem)), which is the same tiny-label-then-large-type rhythm the home hero uses. The portrait's gradient scrim and the name + thesis baked over it were removed entirely — all of it already leads the home hero, and layering it over the photo read as a stock template. Two prior logged decisions were deliberately preserved rather than reversed: the About page head still carries no name (h1 stays visually-hidden), per the existing "About page-head without name" and "About quote without name" entries. Pinned CSS constants updated alongside: ABOUT_GOLD_HEADER_REM became ABOUT_LABEL_REM (0.75) with RETIRED_ABOUT_LABEL_REM (1.5) kept to reject the old value by name, and ABOUT_QUOTE_FONT_SIZE added beside RETIRED_ABOUT_QUOTE_FONT_SIZE. `.bio-full` font-size was deliberately left untouched — it is separately pinned with its own "10% smaller" rationale and was not part of the visual problem. Hero showcase: the page head is now centred and leads with identity.lockedOneLiner at display scale (newly guarded by assertLockedOneLiner, which had no guard before), with the cash-to-digital quote demoted to a deck beneath it, followed by the NYSE interview still as a full-width hero card carrying the name, role, and the three quick facts as glass chips. Consequences accepted deliberately: the 4:5 studio portrait section and the standalone stat-card Quick facts band are both retired, so /portraits/jasper-fu-about.jpg is unused again and each quick fact is published in exactly one place (a test asserts each value and label renders once and that the longer `detail` line, which has no home on a chip, renders nowhere). The showcase reuses the already-guarded MEDIA_KIT_SPEAKING_PHOTO rather than duplicating the asset path. The crop is functional rather than cosmetic — the source still carries a broadcast lower-third across its bottom ~23%, so parseShowcaseAspectRatio pins the frame between 2.32:1 and 3:1 and rejects 16:9 by name, and `height: auto` is pinned alongside it because without it the img's width/height presentational hints make both axes definite and cancel the aspect-ratio entirely. Bio row: the bio had been left alone in a single 42rem column, leaving half the row empty, so it now runs beside the Coinsub company panel exactly as the home brief sets its own biography — the panel reuses `.home-company` through a shared selector rather than duplicating its styling for About. The career timeline and the credentials list, both dot-lists that each previously occupied a half-empty row of their own, now share one two-column band, which also removes a whole section from the page. Media kit: /media-kit was a pass-through (still + heading + a button forwarding to /contact), so it now hosts the inquiry form itself with the type pre-selected to mediaKit. This needed no new mechanism — InquiryForm already accepted a defaultType prop wired to the select's defaultValue and lib/contact.ts already defined MEDIA_KIT_INQUIRY_TYPE; nothing had ever passed them. Hosting the form on the page rather than forwarding to /contact?type=... deliberately avoids reading searchParams, which would have forced /contact from static to dynamic rendering; both routes still build as static. Also fixed a contradiction in live copy: the home media-kit section promised "no request email required" while the only route to the kit is an email request — that sentence was a leftover from the draft copy's download model, which this site already retired when it replaced the "Download Media Kit" CTA (a guard still rejects that label). It now reads "sent on request", and that sentence was extracted from inline JSX into MEDIA_KIT_PROMISE with assertMediaKitPromise, shared by the home section and the /media-kit lede; the guard rejects both the exact retired line and any rewording still containing "no request email required", so the false claim cannot come back. The hero still was then removed from /media-kit entirely: the same NYSE frame already leads the About page and the home page embeds the video of that same interview, so a third outing was overuse, and it also sat short and unbalanced beside a long form. The page is now a single centred column — head centred over the form — which also resolved the earlier two-column attempt. The NYSE still now appears exactly once as an image, on About. The page was then reshaped again: the request form moved into a native <dialog> opened by a button, so /media-kit presents the ask on one centred screen (min-height calc(100dvh - 10rem), measured filling 898px of a 900px viewport) instead of opening on a long form. InquiryForm gained two opt-in props rather than a second component — `types` (narrowed to [mediaKit] here) and `showScheduling` (false here, because Calendly books a conversation and requesting a kit does not need one); /contact passes neither and is unchanged. parseInquiryTypeOptions guards the new prop: it refuses an empty list, duplicates, and a default that is not among the offered options. A native dialog was chosen over a library so Esc-to-close, the focus trap, and the backdrop come from the platform, matching the existing use of <details> for the FAQ and mobile menu; jsdom cannot run showModal(), so open/close, single option, absent Calendly, focus containment, and Esc were all verified in a real browser instead. Known tradeoffs: the response-time note now renders twice in the DOM (under the button and inside the form) though never both on screen at once, and the form is unreachable without JS — it already was, since submitting builds a mailto client-side. The footer still sits below the hero, so the page can scroll to reach it; hiding the footer the way the unlock page does would make it strictly non-scrollable but would cost the legal links. Dialog restyle: the modal now has a bordered head with an × close, a full-bleed footer carrying Cancel beside Send Request, and boxed inputs — the underline treatment gave fields no visible target and left the form reading as a list of labels. The input restyle is deliberately global rather than scoped to the modal, so /contact and the press-alert form match rather than the site carrying two field styles; /contact is otherwise unchanged (still 6 types, Calendly present, submit still full-width via an :only-child rule on the new actions row). The inquiry-type picker is now hidden whenever only one type is offered, inferred from options.length rather than a second prop that could contradict `types` — the value rides along in a hidden input, and a test proves the mailto still routes as Request Media Kit with no picker rendered. Note for future test work: a closed <dialog> is hidden from the accessibility tree in jsdom, so its contents must be asserted through DOM queries, not getByRole. Centring fix: the hero looked off-centre because the generic `article { padding-top: clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.75rem) }` rule started it 70px below the masthead while its min-height still subtracted the full chrome, so centring inside the hero put the ask 34px under the optical centre. Measured rather than eyeballed — gapAbove/gapBelow were 265/197 at 900px and 355/287 at 1080px, a consistent 68px error. Zeroing that padding on .media-kit-page (the same thing `.home` already does) and setting min-height to calc(100dvh - 5.5rem), the masthead's real height, brought both to 231/231 and 321/321. Both values are pinned in identity-css.test.ts with the reason, since restoring the article padding would silently reintroduce the offset. Field pairing: email was full-width and the deadline had been paired with the type picker, so hiding that picker in the modal left the deadline alone on a half-row. Email and deadline are now adjacent half-fields and the type picker moved below them as full-width, which fixes both pages at once — measured by grouping fields on their rendered y-position: modal rows are [Name|Organization], [Email|Deadline], [Notes]; contact rows are [Name|Organization], [Email|Deadline], [Inquiry type], [Notes], with no orphaned half-row on either. The dialog footer's --paper tint was also dropped: it read as a different surface from the form above it, so the divider rule alone separates the actions now, matching the reference. Media coverage: the featured interview on /press/media-coverage was a bordered card with the outlet as plain text; it now uses the same `.featured-interview` split header the home page gives that interview — headline and Nasdaq wordmark left, standfirst and Watch the Interview action right, over a full-width player. No new CSS was needed, the existing rules were already generic. The wordmark is scoped to the featured item on purpose: assertOutletMarkFor has no cleared mark for
, so the remaining three items keep their outlet as text in the card grid. The page test previously asserted only getByText(
) and one iframe title; since the outlet became a logo it now asserts alt/src against assertOutletMarkFor plus title, caption, embed src and watch href, and that the retired card frame and

label are gone. Coverage cards and the Circle link: the Circle entry pointed at https://www.circle.com, which dropped the reader on the corporate home page rather than the interview. Searched, then verified by fetching the page title — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j3MOBy6PUnU is 'Driving Efficiency in Global Payment Systems With USDC | Coinsub (Jasper Fu) | Builder Series', matching the entry exactly, and the thumbnail the user supplied shows the same Builder Series title card. Its kind was corrected from article to video. The three non-featured items now use the press-release card (thumbnail, copy, full-width button) with thumbnails the user added under public/press/. mediaCoverage gained an explicit CoverageItem type so image can be optional — the featured item has none because it runs its player instead. Action labels name the medium (Watch / Listen / Read coverage) rather than the press page's 'Read More', since two of these are videos and one is a podcast. A test now asserts no coverage card links to a bare '/' path, so a repeat of the circle.com case fails rather than shipping; all three destinations were confirmed HTTP 200. Press alerts: the signup was a bare heading with a page-width email field and button stacked under it, because .alert-form sat in the shared stacked-field rule with no width cap. It is now a bordered panel with the ask on the left and the field plus its button inline on the right; .alert-form got its own two-column grid and the label/input pair moved into .alert-form__field, which took .alert-form's place in the stacked rule. Measured in a browser: the input is 403px inside a 1280px panel, sharing a baseline with the button, where it previously spanned the container. Both the panel and the form collapse to one column below 900px. The input also gained aria-invalid and a placeholder; the confirm-signup link became a ghost button so it does not compete with the primary submit. Speaking topics: the list was an <ol> with 01-05 counters, which implied a running order the topics do not have. It is now a <ul> with the same ringed dot the About career timeline uses, rather than a second marker style; the marker column narrowed from 3rem to the dot's own 0.75rem and the now-unused .topic-grid span size rule was dropped. Tests assert the <ol> is gone, the dot count matches speakingTopics.length, and each of 01 through 05 is absent from the page. Booking form: its inputs now use the same boxed treatment as the inquiry and alert forms, and the free-text Date(s) field became a real range — startDate/endDate as native date pickers, with the end picker's min bound to the chosen start. The draft type, empty draft, schema, preview entries (date -> start_date/end_date) and speakingDraftFromBooking all changed with it, and MAX_SPEAKING_DATE was dropped since no free-text date remains. New guards: each date must be a real calendar date, an end date requires a start, and an end cannot precede its start (equal dates are a valid single-day booking). Worth noting: the first implementation validated only the shape with a regex, and a test caught that 2026-13-01 passed it — isSpeakingDate now round-trips the value through Date, which also rejects 2026-02-30 and 2026-11-31. Known gap carried over from the rest of this repo, unrelated to this feature: npm run test:e2e still cannot run on this Windows machine (playwright.config.ts pins a macOS Chrome executablePath), and lib/network-field.ts has one pre-existing lint error (prefer-const) that predates this session and was not touched.
